# ADR-1091: Target the Windows CI leg at what actually broke on Windows

## Status

accepted

## Context

Three issues this reporting session (#633, #634, #636) were all filed by a
Windows end user and all slipped past `ci.yml`. Investigation found a
`test-windows` job already exists (`runs-on: windows-latest`, added
alongside issue #621's fix), running a curated, hand-grown list of eight
test files plus a real `bash scripts/install-plugin.sh` exercise of the
install path. The list grew reactively, one file per Windows bug fixed
("the new file joins the Windows CI leg beside its sibling" -- git history
of commit 7c8def47), never as a recorded scoping decision, and never
included `tests_py/handlers/consolidation/`, where issue #636 lived.

A separate, real gap: this job installs dependencies via
`pip install -r requirements/ci-sqlite-min.txt`, a hash-pinned shortcut
that always carries the `[sqlite]` extra. The real install path
(`install-plugin.sh` -> `scripts/setup.py` -> `ensure_deps()` reading
`launcher_pins.py::BASE_PACKAGES`) never named `sqlite-vec` there -- issue
#634's exact root cause. The job already runs that real path via
`install-plugin.sh`, but nothing checked its output, so the one dependency
gap Windows CI could have caught directly went unchecked regardless.

A first version of this fix replaced the curated list with the full suite,
doubled the job's timeout without a measured basis, and restructured
several steps. The owner rejected that: the curated, additive,
one-file-per-fix pattern is the established convention here, not an
oversight to correct wholesale, and the timeout change had no evidence
behind it. The right fix is additional, targeted verifiers, not a
structural rewrite.

## Decision

Two additive changes only, nothing else in the job's shape or budget
touched.

Add the four existing test files issues #634 and #636 actually changed to
the curated list, following the exact convention already in place:
`tests_py/infrastructure/test_semantic_fallback_169.py` and
`tests_py/test_doctor.py` (#634's sqlite-vec install-and-backfill fix),
`tests_py/handlers/consolidation/test_wiki_maintenance.py` and
`tests_py/handlers/consolidation/test_wiki_backlog_pass.py` (#636's
consolidate-on-SQLite fix). `tests_py/scripts/test_install_plugin_marker_order.py`
(#633's fix, on the still-open, not-yet-merged `fix/issue-633-backend-marker`
branch) is deliberately NOT added here: the file does not exist on `main`
yet, and referencing a nonexistent path would break this job for every
unrelated PR until that branch also merges. Adding it is that branch's own
job, matching the same convention, once it lands.

Add one new step, `scripts/verify_sqlite_extra_parity.py`, run immediately
after `install-plugin.sh`, before the test step. It parses
`pyproject.toml`'s `[sqlite]` extra directly (never a requirements-file
shortcut) and checks each declared package resolves as an installed
distribution under the real install path's own `deps/` directory
(`importlib.metadata.Distribution.discover`, PEP 503 name normalization).
This is the direct, minimal check that would have caught #634: it asserts
against the same install path a real user's machine goes through, not
against a CI-only shortcut that happened to be more complete.

## Consequences

Positive: the Windows leg now runs the actual code both #634 and #636
touched, using the same additive convention the job has always grown by,
so a reviewer reading the diff sees "two files added, one file added, one
new step" rather than a rewritten job. The new verifier directly
regression-tests #634's exact defect class (a `[sqlite]` extra package
declared but not installed by the real path) independent of whatever
individual package caused it next time.

Negative: `tests_py/scripts/test_install_plugin_marker_order.py` is not
yet exercised on Windows CI by this change; it depends on
`fix/issue-633-backend-marker` merging first. The eight-file (now
twelve-file) list remains a hand-maintained convention, not an automated
one -- a future Windows-relevant test file added elsewhere in the tree
still requires a human to remember to add it here, the same limitation
the job already had.
